goal: Given the prompt for a request it is made for, an AI agent does the task as the prompt's writer means, with only what its run gives it, on every run and in cases the writer did not foresee.

parts.what: What the host reads to choose the prompt for a request: a name that says what the prompt does, and a description of what it does and the requests it is used for.
The tools the AI may use, listed where the host reads them and refuses any other, when the host allows such a list.
What the AI reads first in the body: what it is to achieve, for whom, how it knows it is done, and what lies outside its task.
What the AI needs and cannot find or know on its own: the situation, its inputs and where they are, and the rules of this place.
The steps in the order the AI takes them, each step the result that holds when it ends, with the rules the step needs, each with its reason, or the script that does it and how to run it.
What the AI hands back, in what form, and to whom.

The trials that try the prompt: one case for each class of input and each rule of its steps, where the AI must act and where it must not; the set-up of each case, the stand-ins for the person and for the prompt's neighbours, the judges, and the checks made on each run's record.

benefits.what: When the AI believes it has finished, can it tell from the prompt whether it has reached what the task is for?
When the AI meets a choice that is the user's, such as one between options that serve equally or an action hard to undo, does it hand the choice to the user rather than make it?
Given the prompt and only what its run gives it, can the AI do each step without guessing a fact, such as where its inputs are or a rule of the place it works in?
Taking the steps in order, does the AI arrive at what the goal says the task is for, with no step that leads it elsewhere?
When the AI meets a case a step's rule does not name, can it decide the case as the writer would, from the reason the rule gives?
When the AI is run twice on the same input, does each step whose result must not vary, such as a check or a file's form, give the same result both times?
Can the AI take every action its steps call for with the tools it is allowed?
When the AI, during a run, reaches for an action that lies outside its task, does the host refuse it?
When the caller, the person or the AI that started the prompt, takes what the AI hands back, can it act on it without asking the AI anything further?

When a request the prompt is made for comes, and a request near it that it is not made for, does the host, such as Claude Code, choose the prompt for the first and pass it over for the second, from the name and the description alone?
Once the host has chosen the prompt by its description, does the AI do the task the description says, all of it and nothing more?
When the prompt is run several times on each kind of request it is made for, does the AI reach the result the prompt names on every run?
Does every line of the prompt change what the AI does toward the task, so that none draws its attention from the lines that do?
For each rule of the steps, where the AI must act and where it must not, can the maintainer point to the trial case that tries it, and see from that case's record that the situation it tries arose?
When a trial fails, can the maintainer tell from its record that the prompt went wrong and not the trial: its set-up, a stand-in, a judge or a check?
When the maintainer takes out of the prompt what a trial case tries, does that case fail?
When the AI puts a decision, a proposal or a report to the person, can the person approve or decide from its first lines alone, and reach the details only where they ask?
When the caller acts on what the AI reports it did or found, does each claim hold as far as the report says it was checked?
